posts:
Left-wing legislation fills the congressional hopper as progressive lawmakers prep for a new majority.
Evidence: Bill filings, Pressley proposals, ICE funding cuts
#Aletheia #USPol 🌐

House Democrats are readying a blitz of progressive bills, including decriminalizing prostitution and defunding ICE, as incoming socialist lawmakers prepare to enter Congress.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Greater Good

While specific progressive bills are filed, partisan framing weaponizes policy proposals to stoke fear of radical upheaval rather than evaluating legislative merit.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.93, -0.86) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.5, Uncertainty z: 3)
House Democrats are introducing progressive bills such as ending the federal death penalty and cutting ICE funding, reflecting shifting congressional dynamics.

The Poison:
Framing routine policy disagreement as a hostile takeover weaponizes anxiety for partisan engagement rather than informing voters.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The reporting conflates standard legislative filings by individual representatives with an apocalyptic 'storm' by extremists.

Social Physics Analysis:
Tabloids run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by dressing up standard policy filings as an invading threat. This manufactured crisis deflects from actual legislative debate to harvest outrage clicks and fuel partisan tribalism.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
Modal Dynamics: can be -> Won't be via Red Top (The Imperial Trap).
When routine policy proposals are reframed as existential invasions, open democratic capacity is inverted into manufactured fear.

The Unavoidable Truth: Lawmakers are indeed filing progressive bills for the upcoming congressional session.

The Unavoidable Lie: The hyperbolic framing implies an illegitimate 'storming' rather than standard legislative process.

Alethekanon:
Sensationalized framing turns routine legislative proposals into manufactured panic, prioritizing outrage over sober policy analysis.

Awwthekanon:
It is exhausting when political reporting chooses fear over understanding, pitting neighbors against each other instead of encouraging constructive dialogue on tough issues.

It's just politicians filing bills like they always do, but the headline acts like Congress is getting raided by sci-fi villains.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Dem lawmakers already filling hopper with far left bills as socialists prepare to storm DC

Want to know what a left-wing driven Congress that will gavel into session in January will do? Look at some of the bills lefty lawmakers have already introduced in the current one.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

House Democrats are prepping a blitz of far-left bills—including decriminalizing prostitution and axing ICE — as a newly empowered majority and a surge of socialist lawmakers look to ram long-stalled legislation through Congress.

Original “Squad” member Rep. Ayanna Pressley (D-Mass.) has bills  to end the federal death penalty and decriminalize prostitution, which she has called a “byproduct of discrimination, poverty and/or addiction.”

Pressley will be joined by eight new incoming lawmakers who are members of the Democratic Socialists of America and who are getting ready to flex their muscle, although their experience in elected office varies.

Her “People’s Justice Guarantee” is meant to combat mass incarceration and expand access to “restorative justice,” which critics have bashed as a lenient, criminal-first approach to justice.

The newbies are expected to draw from the DSA’s platform –- which commits all endorsed candidates to backing its radical agenda. A DSA electoral commission document reviewed by The Post sets up a “Socialists-In-Office” network to collaborate with winners “towards the goal of promoting Democratic Socialism.”

The progressive onslaught extends far beyond DSA-backed lawmakers like Pressley.

Rep. Yvette Clarke (D-NY) wants to boost “diversity visas” after President Trump slashed thousands from the program that sprinkles 55,000 US work visas around the globe.

Outgoing Rep. Nydia Velazquez (D-NY) has a bill to provide training to business owners on resisting ICE — a proposal that comes after a campaign season in which a host of candidates called to eliminate or defund the immigration enforcement agency. Velazquez is being succeeded by democratic socialist Claire Valdez, who has called for a “living wage” and talked up her own time working low-wage jobs at Taco Bell.

Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.) has introduced the “Drain ICE Act” to rescind $75 billion in funds the agency got under Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM) has introduced a resolution “recognizing the disparity in wages paid to Latinas and the impact of that disparity on women, families, the economy, and the United States.”
